name: Spirit (MER-A)
keyDiscovery: Spirit found silica deposits near Home Plate that could only have formed in hot springs or steam vents, providing the strongest evidence yet for past hydrothermal environments on Mars.
missionLegacy: Spirit proved that a 90-day rover could survive over six years on Mars, and its discovery of hydrothermal signatures reshaped the search for habitable environments beyond Earth.
funFact: Spirit's broken front wheel accidentally became its best science tool — dragging through the soil, it uncovered nearly pure silica that pointed to ancient hot springs.
heritageNote: Spirit is permanently embedded in soft soil at a site called Troy near Home Plate in Gusev Crater; it last communicated on 22 March 2010 and was declared lost on 25 May 2011.

objects.name: Spirit Rover
objects.description: Spirit landed in Gusev Crater on 4 January 2004 for a planned 90-sol mission, but operated for over six years. In 2009, its right front wheel became stuck in soft soil at a site called 'Troy'. NASA spent months trying to free it before declaring Spirit a stationary research platform. Last contact was 22 March 2010.
objects.scienceDiscovery: Discovered nearly pure silica deposits and goethite minerals proving ancient hydrothermal activity — hot springs or steam vents — once existed at Gusev Crater.
objects.legacy: Spirit is stuck in soft soil at Troy, tilted with its solar panels unable to catch enough winter sun; it has been silent since 22 March 2010.
objects.firstPerson: Yo, talk about pure grit! I am Spirit — MER-A! NASA planned a 90-sol mission, but I survived for over six grueling years across Gusev Crater! I fought through raging dust storms, survived brutal freezing winters, and climbed entire mountains on six wheels. They called me Spirit because you literally could not break my resolve!

objects.name: Columbia Hills
objects.description: Spirit drove 3 km to reach the Columbia Hills, named for the seven astronauts lost in the Space Shuttle Columbia disaster. The hills proved to be a scientific treasure: Spirit found evidence that water had once altered the rocks here. Minerals like goethite and hematite confirmed past water activity.
objects.scienceDiscovery: Contained rocks altered by water, including goethite (an iron mineral that only forms in the presence of water), proving Gusev Crater once had liquid water.
objects.legacy: The Columbia Hills remain a memorial to the seven Space Shuttle Columbia astronauts; Spirit's exploration showed their namesake hills held profound scientific secrets.
objects.firstPerson: Bro, look at this view! I am the Columbia Hills — named in eternal tribute to the seven heroes of Space Shuttle Columbia. Spirit drove 3 kilometers across treacherous dunes just to reach my peaks and uncover ancient rocks soaked in ancient hot springs. Monument of courage on Mars!

objects.name: Home Plate Formation
objects.description: Home Plate is a roughly circular plateau about 80 metres across in the Inner Basin of the Columbia Hills. Spirit found that it was composed of layered rocks with a volcanic origin, likely formed by explosive interaction between magma and water or ice. This was strong evidence for past hydrothermal activity.
objects.scienceDiscovery: Revealed layered volcanic rocks formed by explosive interaction between magma and water or ice — strong evidence for past hydrothermal activity on Mars.
objects.legacy: Home Plate is recognised as one of the most scientifically significant geological formations discovered by any Mars rover.
objects.firstPerson: Ayo, baseball fans on Mars! I am Home Plate — an 80-meter plateau of layered volcanic ash. Spirit spent two harsh Martian winters parked on my slopes, discovering silica-rich deposits that proved boiling hydrothermal geysers once exploded right here. Mars had hot springs, baby!

objects.name: Rover Wheel Tracks
objects.description: Spirit's broken right front wheel, which stopped turning in 2006, inadvertently became a scientific tool. As Spirit dragged the wheel, it scraped away the surface layer to reveal bright white soil rich in silica — up to 90% pure SiO₂. This discovery suggested either hot springs or fumaroles once existed here.
objects.scienceDiscovery: Accidentally uncovered soil that was 90% pure silica — a composition that on Earth forms only in hot springs or volcanic steam vents.
objects.legacy: The wheel tracks exposing silica remain on the surface, a visible record of one of Mars exploration's most serendipitous discoveries.
objects.firstPerson: Bro, greatest accidental discovery in space history! In 2006, Spirit's right front wheel broke and stopped spinning, dragging behind like an anchor. But that dragged wheel scraped away the topsoil and revealed 90 percent pure silica — proof of ancient hydrothermal vents! A broken wheel unlocked the biggest scientific jackpot of the mission. Infinite aura!

objects.name: Bonneville Crater
objects.description: Bonneville Crater was one of Spirit's first major waypoints, a 200-metre impact crater about 300 metres from the landing site. Scientists hoped to find exposed rock layers in its walls, but found mostly loose soil. The disappointment led to the decision to drive the 3 km to Columbia Hills — which turned out to be the right call.
objects.scienceDiscovery: Showed that not all craters expose useful rock layers, which redirected the mission toward the far more rewarding Columbia Hills.
objects.legacy: Bonneville Crater remains an unremarkable impact feature, but it played a pivotal role in the decision that made the Spirit mission legendary.
objects.firstPerson: Look down into the abyss! I am Bonneville Crater — a 200-meter impact bowl that Spirit explored early in her mission. Looking into my fractured rim gave geologists their first peek beneath Gusev Crater's dusty volcanic crust. Classic impact architecture!

objects.name: Backshell and Parachute
objects.description: Spirit's backshell and parachute landed about 300 metres from the rover. The airbag-enclosed lander bounced 28 times before coming to rest. These entry, descent, and landing components remain on the Martian surface as testament to the engineering that delivered Spirit safely to Gusev Crater.
objects.scienceDiscovery: No direct science, but the EDL hardware demonstrates the airbag landing technology that delivered two rovers safely to Mars.
objects.legacy: The backshell and parachute remain on the surface about 300 metres from Spirit's landing site, visible in orbital imagery.
objects.firstPerson: Bro, I took the fiery heat so Spirit could live! I am the backshell and supersonic parachute. I slammed into Mars' upper atmosphere at 19,000 kilometers per hour, enduring 1,500 degrees of friction before popping the parachute and drifting softly down. A twisted pile of heroic metal resting proudly in the red sands!
